title: Jaws Bridge, Edgartown, Massachusetts
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Jaws Bridge, Edgartown, Massachusetts
excerpt: Planning a charter bus to Jaws Bridge on Martha's Vineyard? The ferry decides everything — why most groups leave the coach on the mainland, and what it costs.

heroImage.alt: The low concrete span of the American Legion Memorial Bridge between Edgartown and Oak Bluffs

extraImage.alt: The channel and beach either side of Jaws Bridge on Martha's Vineyard in summer

body.text: The American Legion Memorial Bridge carries a two-lane road between Edgartown and Oak Bluffs, and almost nobody calls it that. In 1975 Steven Spielberg filmed the estuary scene here, and ever since it has been Jaws Bridge — a low concrete span that people queue up to jump off in summer. Getting a group there involves one decision that governs everything else, and a charter bus to Jaws Bridge is really a question about the ferry.
The ferry decides the whole trip

Martha's Vineyard is an island. Every vehicle that reaches it does so on a Steamship Authority ferry from Woods Hole, and space for large vehicles is limited, expensive, and booked far in advance. Taking a full-size coach across is possible and it is rarely the right answer.

What most groups do instead: the charter carries everyone to the Woods Hole terminal, the group walks onto the ferry as foot passengers, and island transport handles the rest. Walk-on tickets are inexpensive, need no vehicle reservation, and the crossing takes about forty-five minutes. The coach either waits at Woods Hole or returns to collect you in the evening, and both arrangements are cheaper than shipping it across.

Tell your operator which arrangement you want when you ask for a price. A quote assuming the vehicle waits eight hours at the terminal is a different number from one assuming it drives away and comes back, and the difference is worth knowing about before you commit.
The bridge itself, and the jumping

It is a modest structure — that is part of the charm. The water below is a tidal channel between Sengekontacket Pond and Nantucket Sound, and jumping from the bridge has been an island summer ritual for decades. It has also produced injuries, the current runs hard on a changing tide, and depth varies.

If you are bringing a youth group, decide your position on this before you arrive rather than at the railing with thirty teenagers watching other people jump. The photograph from the bridge is the reason to come, and it does not require anybody to get wet.
What else to do on the island

items: Oak Bluffs: the gingerbread cottages of the Methodist Campground, and the Flying Horses Carousel, the oldest operating platform carousel in the country. A ten-minute walk from the bridge's northern end.
Edgartown: whaling captains' houses, white clapboard and picket fences, and the harbour. The prettiest town on the island and the most walkable.
Aquinnah Cliffs: coloured clay cliffs and a lighthouse at the western tip, about forty minutes from Edgartown.
State Beach: the stretch of sand running either side of the bridge, calm on the pond side and open on the Sound side.

body.text: Which charter bus fits the mainland leg

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/charter-buses) is right for the run down from Boston or Providence to Woods Hole, with luggage bays for an overnight group.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) is the more practical vehicle if you do intend to take it across, and considerably cheaper on the ferry.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) crosses easily and suits a small group that wants a vehicle on the island.

body.text: Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for a Vineyard trip should raise the island question in the first conversation. An operator who quotes without asking how you intend to cross has not planned the trip, and the ferry is the expensive, capacity-constrained part.
Getting to the ferry

Woods Hole is the year-round vehicle port and sits at the tip of Cape Cod near [Falmouth](/locations/massachusetts/falmouth), around ninety minutes from [Boston](/locations/massachusetts/boston) without traffic and considerably more on a summer Friday. Seasonal fast ferries also run from [Hyannis](/locations/massachusetts/hyannis) and [New Bedford](/locations/massachusetts/new-bedford), both of which are passenger-only and often the simpler option for a walk-on group.
Build in a real buffer. Cape traffic in July and August is genuinely bad, ferries leave on time, and a group that misses a sailing waits for the next one.

One detail worth knowing before you plan a summer visit: the bridge area has very limited parking of its own, and what exists fills early. Groups arriving as foot passengers and using island transport avoid the problem entirely, which is another argument for leaving the coach at Woods Hole rather than shipping it across.
When to go

June and September are the sweet spot: the island is fully open, the water is warm enough, and the crowds are manageable. July and August are the busiest and the hardest for ferry space. From late October the island winds down substantially, with many restaurants and businesses closed until spring, which suits a quiet off-season trip and disappoints anyone expecting the summer version.
Booking the trip

Send your date, headcount, departure point and which ferry you intend to take. Our [event transportation](/services/event-transportation) team routinely schedules Cape and island trips around sailing times rather than around the drive.
